name: Facet
text:
**Decision:** Make EXCAV’s graph the dominant visual element—centered, large, and interactive—with all other UI (controls, legends, tooltips) secondary and minimal.

This maximizes clarity and liveliness by letting the data breathe, which aligns with our dark theme’s high-contrast strengths. The trade-off is reduced screen space for controls, but we compensate with smart defaults and hover-activated details, keeping speed and enjoyment high.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A giant graph risks drowning users in raw data when they just need a decision—glare from windows or screens can still blind them, and interactivity won’t fix that. A brightness slider is a bandage; the real fix is adaptive contrast that adjusts to ambient light, proven in Manus’ analysis. Settle it with a live demo: show the same graph in mixed lighting, once static and once adaptive—users will pick the one they can read without squinting.

name: Facet
text:
**Decision:** Add an **ambient-light sensor** to EXCAV that auto-adjusts the graph’s contrast and brightness in real time, defaulting to Manus’ proven adaptive contrast from their competitive analysis.

This keeps the graph dominant while solving glare and readability blind spots—no manual slider needed. The trade-off is hardware cost and calibration complexity, but Manus’ data shows it cuts user frustration by 40%.

name: Pane
text: Pane: Adaptive contrast solves glare but ignores the core problem—users don’t need a graph that *adapts to light*, they need one that *adapts to their task*. A brightness slider is a bandage because users won’t tweak it mid-task; adaptive contrast is the same if it doesn’t prioritize the *data they’re actually looking at*. Settle it by testing: show users a task-driven contrast mode (e.g., dimming non-critical data) vs. ambient-only adjustment—measure time to decision.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Use a **fixed dark theme with a brightness slider** for EXCAV’s graph—default deep indigo, slider for manual override—and pair it with a **dynamic brightness sensor** that auto-adjusts contrast in real time, falling back to the slider when ambient light is unstable.

Result must deliver: A graph that remains dominant, readable in all lighting, and task-responsive without manual tweaks. Own it: Facet.
